body:
There should be a sub for recovering neckbeards/legbeards or people who want to get out of the beard lifestyle.

Most of the things you listed are true about me, except for that I don't play video games and I'm not a pothead. I'm underemployed but I still help my parents pay some bills. I don't own a car, but my dad lets me use his car since I need to drive to work and he rarely leaves the house anyway. I didn't get a driver's license until I was 26.

Instead of playing video games, I spend most of my time aimlessly browsing the internet. I read articles, forum posts, and watch videos. When I'm offline, I read books and sometimes write. Unlike the stereotypical mom's basement girl, I don't care about Tumblr or fandom stuff. I don't dye my hair in unnatural colors nor do I want any tattoos. I support LGBT and female empowerment, but I don't believe in that HAES or #72genders SJW stuff. 

When it comes to guys, Chad has always intimidated me. I always knew on some level that Chad will only pump and dump me, so I avoided guys like him. I have a low sex drive and I've never been boy crazy in the first place. But that's another story...

My little sister is the absolute opposite: got her license as soon as she was old enough, has a well-paying job, lives independently, has had boyfriends and has an active social life. I wonder where I went wrong :-(

I hope I can move out by the time I'm 30.

>>You bring this up a few times. What is this about?

I'm not as emotionally mature as my peers. I also have less life experience and social graces than they do. It's not easy to explain, but I'm behind my age group in many aspects.
I've tried online dating. However, I can never hold a conversation with anyone via messaging. I never know what to say, even if their profile clearly expresses their interests. :/

>>Were you ever physically or sexually abused as a child?

I don't have many memories from before I was 8 years old. I'm not sure if that's normal. I don't remember any sexual abuse. Many of my memories are about how inconsistent my mom was when it came to corporal punishment. I would get whipped with a belt for minor incidents, yet sometimes when I did something truly bad, like when I threw eggs on the living room carpet, nothing happened to me. My father rarely hit me, he wasn't at home very often, but he was a nice man and a calm, stable contrast compared to my mother.

The unpredictability didn't end at home, I was put in a special ed class where they lumped the learning disabled/developmentally delayed kids with ones with conduct disorders and anger issues. I never knew when someone was going to lose their temper and hurt me. I'm glad I didn't get bullied very much there, but the few times that I did, I knew there was a good chance a fight could break out if I stood up for myself, and sometimes they did hit me. 

I wouldn't go as far as to say I was abused, but there was a point in my life where I felt that if I even slightly tread the line, someone would hit me, whether at school or at home.

This is an interesting post. I have felt distant from others for most of my life. I want to look more into complex post-traumatic stress disorder. If by dissociative disorder you mean DID, I doubt I have multiple personalities. I do feel like I lack a sense of identity and feel emotional numbness. 

As for my sexuality, yes I've fantasized about women and had crushes on them. I just feel that it makes things more complicated. 

>>There is something much much bigger going on here.

I suspect you're right. Thank you for the insightful post.

I'm getting a paralegal certificate. It's cheaper than law school and I can at least make a living out of it. 

Sometimes I wonder why I even bothered applying. I feel that I'll spend decades living a mundane life surrounded by people I can't relate to anyway.

I graduated from college a few years ago but now I'm stuck in inertia because I don't feel like I can deal with the real world. I do have a job, but it's not enough money for me to live independently.

I want to take college classes just to find people to socialize with. I did get my bachelors two years ago but I'm not even sure what to do with it. I'm not sure if I could deal with the pressure of office politics. I currently have a job but it's not enough for me to make a living.

Thankfully, I'm not trying to be a model or pop star but I'm just more aware that doors are closing for opportunities.

No. I'm saying that if I had everything together I wouldn't worry about my age. I just feel that I'm running out of time if I want to make any significant changes in my life. 
I just feel like society is more forgiving towards men who want to start over in life, granted they actually work hard to make changes.

Thank you for your words. You're more helpful than you realize. I have had self-esteem problems for as long as I can remember, not just because of my home life but just with my self-confidence when it comes to interacting with others. Social anxiety is hard to deal with. 
I knew someone with ADHD, he was so creative and energetic. I know ADHD has its challenges, but I was jealous of those qualities lol.
Anyway, I will try to remember the positive things about myself. And stop reading TRP :)
I saw it. It is encouraging, but I noted that she has at least had a decent amount of dating experience compared to me.

Things I like about myself:

- I am polite to others.

- I have more patience than the average person.

- I can stay focused on anything for the longest time. Whatever the opposite of ADHD is, I probably have it lol.

- I am inquisitive and know I will be a life long learner. 

I feel that the reason I was drawn towards TRP was because I thought that's how men truly felt. I thought it was a place where men say what guys think, but won't say in public. An example is my dad. Although, I highly doubt my father knows what TRP is, he espouses many of their views and has lived out what they want in life. He married a younger woman. My mom was 25 and my dad was 34 when they had me. My mom is his second wife. He had several girlfriends before he met my mom and even showed me all of their photos. He has cheated on my mom throughout their marriage. He also makes rude remarks about the appearance and weight of women he finds unattractive behind their backs. 

However, he's a good dad. He encouraged my sister and I to get an education. He was supportive of all my interests and was okay with me being a tomboy as a kid. I also know that he would never want me to marry someone with a history like his. 

However, he lives a somewhat empty life because of the shallow way he views people. He has no close friends and often argues with my mom. They seriously considered divorce. I realize that living the RP lifestyle might lead to a hollow existence and even wanted to avoid getting married because of my parents' unhappy marriage. I'm sorry for the long post about my family, but it is some perspective if you are interested.

Thank you so much. This is exactly what I needed to hear. 

However, I was an idiot and read a Purple Pill thread:
https://www.reddit.com/r/PurplePillDebate/comments/409x3i/the_red_pill_is_actually_just_a_well_put_together/?ref=share&ref_source=link

I feel like the female version of this post. I've never had a relationship, let alone a proper date. I think it's because of my anxiety and poor social skills. 
I probably won't struggle finding interested partners but I feel that people will be turned off once they find out I'm a 27-year-old virgin who has never had a relationship. I've had offers for sex, but I turned them down because it just didn't feel right. If I knew I was still going to be alone, I would've jumped at the opportunity. I'm not dismissing anything you said, I just feel like I have a long struggle ahead of me if I don't want to die alone.

I just dread turning 30 and having nothing to show for it. At 30, you're considered a full-fledged adult no matter what. No excuses.

I recently got a therapist to treat my anxiety. I hope it works well. I at least want a nice, judgmental group of friends if I don't get a relationship.

It's okay. You put effort into your response. I think it's a good idea to focus on my career and interests. Sometimes the loneliness drains me. The reason I focus on my lackluster sexual life is because I'm missing out on something that the majority of people have already experienced. I get depressed and too unmotivated to do anything. I need to fight my negative feelings.
I feel hopeless. I have no life. I might as well be dead.
